title: Schmigadoon! Won 2026's Best Musical — But Is It Too Insider for You? Watch Roma's Review!
transcript: >> If you're going to parody Broadway musicals, you'd better know what makes them tick. And happily, Schmigadoon knows exactly what it's doing. That's why it won the Tony for best musical. Adapted from the beloved TV series, this exuberant production harkens back to the golden age of Broadway, lovingly skewering familiar conventions while simultaneously embracing them. The result, one of the cleverest and most entertaining musical comedies on Broadway in years. The story spoofs Brigadoon, the Lerner and Loewe musical about an enchanted village where magical things happen. Alex Brightman and Sarah Chase play a bickering couple who stumble into the mythical Schmigadoon, where they discover everyone breaks into song. Show creator Cinco Paul pulled a bravura hat trick writing the book, music, and lyrics, and it's all meticulously crafted with wit to spare. Paul's melodies are both delightfully familiar and freshly original, and he clearly understands that effective satire begins with genuine admiration. Director-choreographer Christopher Gattelli balances affectionate homage with broad comedy. His inventive staging never loses sight of the story's emotional core, and his choreography is equally sharp, capturing the distinctive dance styles from so many iconic shows. The cast is exceptional. Everyone finds the sweet spot between sincerity and satire. Brightman singing just one song is sensational, wringing every possible laugh as the musical averse Josh Skinner. And Sarah Chase is equally sublime as his musical-loving girlfriend, Melissa Gimble. Amid all the cleverness lies a heartfelt message, reminding us why these classic musicals have endured for generations. Beneath the corny spectacle, they're all about the transformative power of love and self-discovery. Schmigadoon will mostly appeal to musical theater fans. They'll be in heaven picking up on all the insider references. It's not a show for everyone, but even those who can't distinguish Rodgers from Hammerstein are likely to find themselves charmed and humming all the way home.
